target.incomplete: Only the verifications that ran are covered here. A migration is confirmed when both the files and the database have been compared.
target.sourceServer: Source (where the files are read from)
target.targetServer: Target (where it is brought back up)
target.steps: Steps, in order, with what each must produce
target.dbBody: The dump is taken inside the container on the source, moved as one file, and restored on the target. The table count and the row counts of a bounded sample decide whether the restore is complete — a partial restore fails loudly.
target.needDryRun: A dry run must pass (PASS) before the restore can run.
target.dryBanner: Dry run: these are the exact commands. Nothing has been written — no directory, no dump, no restore.
target.dbCancelled: Cancelled. The dump on both ends is kept, so running it again resumes — nothing was restored.
target.dbVerification: After: {{tables}} tables, {{sampled}} sampled row counts compared, dump sha256 {{digest}}.
target.bringUpBody: A checklist, not a conversation: .env, dependencies, build, two PM2 apps, the nginx sites, the certificates and a health check on each port. Every step shows its command, what success looks like, and a verdict — and it can be cancelled and resumed.
target.domains: Domains that need a certificate — their DNS must already point at the target
target.resume: Continue from the steps that passed
target.stopping: Stopping at the next step boundary — the steps that already passed are kept.
target.runCancelled: Cancelled. The steps that passed are kept — Continue resumes from there instead of starting over.
target.envReport: .env keys (presence only — a value is never read)
